note: Implementation-defined intent taxonomy. Labels must be lowercase snake_case and 'unknown' must remain. 'tactics' are the MITRE ATT&CK tactics (x_mitre_shortname) each intent investigates; together the intents cover the eight evaluation tactics of the paper (execution, persistence, privilege escalation, defense evasion, credential access, discovery, lateral movement, impact). ATT&CK v20 split defense evasion into 'stealth' and 'defense-impairment', so defense_evasion lists all three. Each relevant evidence category is either critical ('critical_evidence') or supporting (the rest), as in the paper's ontology (Section 6.1).

intents.label: suspicious_process_execution
intents.name: Suspicious process execution
intents.description: Unusual or suspicious process creation, script or command execution on an endpoint whose purpose is not yet established.

intents.label: malware_investigation
intents.name: Malware investigation
intents.description: Suspected malicious file or binary present or executed on a system (excluding ransomware, which has its own label).

intents.label: ransomware_investigation
intents.name: Ransomware investigation
intents.description: Mass file encryption, ransom notes, shadow-copy deletion or other indicators of ransomware.

intents.label: phishing_investigation
intents.name: Phishing investigation
intents.description: Suspicious or malicious email, links or attachments delivered to users.

intents.label: credential_compromise
intents.name: Credential compromise
intents.description: Brute force, password spraying, credential theft or suspicious use of valid accounts.

intents.label: lateral_movement
intents.name: Lateral movement
intents.description: An adversary moving between internal systems, e.g. via remote services, admin shares or remote execution.

intents.label: privilege_escalation
intents.name: Privilege escalation
intents.description: An adversary gaining higher privileges on a system, e.g. UAC bypass, exploited services, token manipulation or new privileged accounts.

intents.label: defense_evasion
intents.name: Defense evasion
intents.description: Disabling or tampering with security tools, clearing logs, obfuscated scripts, masquerading or proxy execution to avoid detection.

intents.label: discovery
intents.name: Discovery
intents.description: Reconnaissance from inside the environment: system, account, group, process, share or network enumeration.

intents.label: data_exfiltration
intents.name: Data exfiltration
intents.description: Unauthorised transfer of data out of the environment.

intents.label: system_impact
intents.name: Destructive impact
intents.description: Destruction or disruption other than ransomware encryption: data or disk wiping, stopped services, inhibited recovery, defacement or removed accounts.

intents.label: denial_of_service
intents.name: Denial of service / availability
intents.description: Attacks degrading availability, such as volumetric DDoS or resource exhaustion.

intents.label: web_application_attack
intents.name: Web application attack
intents.description: Exploitation attempts against web applications, e.g. SQL injection, web shells or path traversal.

intents.label: command_and_control_persistence
intents.name: Command-and-control or persistence
intents.description: Beaconing to adversary infrastructure or mechanisms that keep adversary access (run keys, scheduled tasks, services).

intents.label: unknown
intents.name: Unknown / insufficient information
intents.description: The incident does not contain enough information to determine an intent with reasonable confidence.
